case: Withdrawn record; the DOI resolves to a Zenodo tombstone page
note: ADR-0027: withdrawn records are KEPT. The raw payload is a real Zenodo 410 tombstone body and it carries no metadata at all — which is exactly why a tombstone must never be scraped. A scraped event replaces the source block wholesale, so scraping this would blank the record. The adapter detects it (ZenodoAdapter.is_tombstone) and skips it in harvest(); withdrawal is appended as a `withdrawn` event against the identity the caller already holds (ZenodoAdapter.recheck_withdrawn, runbook handle-a-withdrawn-record). The resulting record keeps its metadata, its URL and CKAN state=active, with lifecycle_state/withdrawn/withdrawn_at carrying the withdrawal.
invented: The RAW PAYLOAD IS REAL — captured verbatim from https://zenodo.org/api/records/5890532 on 2026-08-31, HTTP 410, a record Zenodo staff removed as spam. The record it is attached to is the invented zen-01 reference identity (10.5281/zenodo.1234566), deliberately: marking a real IEA Wind artifact as withdrawn would be a lie about someone's work.
